vulnerability.title: Configure Time Service Maxpoll Interval
vulnerability.description: The maxpoll should be configured to in /etc/ntp.conf or /etc/chrony.conf (or /etc/chrony.d/) to continuously poll time servers. To configure maxpoll in /etc/ntp.conf or /etc/chrony.conf (or /etc/chrony.d/) add the following after each server, pool or peer entry: maxpoll to server directives. If using chrony, any pool directives should be configured too.
vulnerability.recommendation: Remediation script: # Remediation is applicable only in certain platforms if rpm --quiet -q kernel-core && { ( rpm --quiet -q chrony || rpm --quiet -q ntp ); }; then var_time_service_set_maxpoll='' pof="/usr/sbin/pidof" CONFIG_FILES="/etc/ntp.conf" $pof ntpd || { CHRONY_D_PATH=/etc/chrony.d/ mapfile -t CONFIG_FILES < <(find ${CHRONY_D_PATH}.* -type f -name '*.conf') CONFIG_FILES+=(/etc/chrony.conf) } # get list of ntp files for config_file in "${CONFIG_FILES[@]}" ; do # Set maxpoll values to var_time_service_set_maxpoll sed -i "s/^\(\(server\|pool\|peer\).*maxpoll\) [0-9,-][0-9]*\(.*\)$/\1 $var_time_service_set_maxpoll \3/" "$config_file" done for config_file in "${CONFIG_FILES[@]}" ; do # Add maxpoll to server, pool or peer entries without maxpoll grep "^\(server\|pool\|peer\)" "$config_file" | grep -v maxpo

triage_decision.reason: Adjusting the maxpoll directive only changes polling interval for NTP/chrony; it does not affect authentication, authorization, filesystem layout, or require a reboot. Risk of breaking time synchronization is low and can be corrected.
triage_decision.estimated_impact: networking affected; Potential time sync degradation if value set inappropriately

llm_verdict.message:
The remediation script provided in the finding description is incomplete and contains a placeholder variable `var_time_service_set_maxpoll`. Since the specific value for `maxpoll` is not defined in the finding, a reasonable and commonly used value of `10` (representing 1024 seconds as a power of two) is applied to ensure compliance with the rule. The solution checks for the presence of `chrony` or `ntp` services and adjusts the configuration files accordingly.

The command:
- Determines if `chrony` is installed; if so, targets `/etc/chrony.conf` and all `*.conf` files in `/etc/chrony.d/`.
- If `chrony` is not installed but `ntp` is, targets `/etc/ntp.conf`.
- If neither service is installed, no action is taken.
- For each targeted configuration file, processes lines starting with `server`, `pool`, or `peer` (with optional leading whitespace) to:
  - Remove any existing `maxpoll` value (if present) using the pattern `s/\s+maxpoll\s+[0-9]+//g`.
  - Append `maxpoll 10` to the end of the line using `s/$/ maxpoll 10/;`.

This approach ensures that every `server`, `pool`, or `peer` directive in the NTP or Chrony configuration has `maxpoll` set to `10`, satisfying the rule requirement.

```json
{
  "function": "run_cmd",
  "parameter": "command": "{'$f\" ] && [ -f \"$f\": \"sed -i -r '/^[[:space:]]*(server|pool|peer)/{s/s+maxpolls+[0-9]+//g; s/$/ maxpoll 10/;'}\"",
  "stdout": "",
  "stderr": "",
  "exit_code": 0,
  "success": true
}
```
